On a nonempty connected open set $O$ in the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], select one smooth future timelike Killing field $\xi$ and one smooth scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ in kelvins. Its dimensionless lapse and selected observer congruence are

$$N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0,\qquad u:=\xi/N_\xi.$$

Thus $g(u,u)=-1$ and the physical four-velocity is $cu$ in the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. A reference normalization of $\xi$ is part of the selected model. The local temperature $T$ is assigned to this comoving observer congruence; it is not a coordinate temperature or a value assigned to every observer.

Adopt the inverse-temperature vector

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},$$

where $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, and assume that this field is Killing on $O$. In this item, a selected stationary thermal equilibrium means precisely this adopted bath, observer congruence, positive proper-temperature field, and Killing condition on $\beta$. The field $N_\xi T$ is not assumed constant here; its constancy is the conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]].

This is a model assumption, not a statement that every stationary geometry admits a thermal state or that every material realizes this bath. It asserts no complete Killing flow, KMS state, trace-class stress exponential, collision or thermalization law, Hawking or Unruh temperature, or empirical thermometer reading.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

derivations.claim: By [A1], $O$ is connected, $\xi$ is future timelike Killing, $T$ is smooth and strictly positive, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ is Killing. These are the carrier and field hypotheses in [F1].

Apply the forward implication of [F1] to the fields from step 1.1. It gives a positive constant $T_K$ on all of $O$ with $N_\xi T=T_K$ and $ eta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, along with $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, $a=
abla\log N_\xi$, and zero expansion and shear. Since $T=T_K/N_\xi$ and both fields are smooth and positive, differentiating its logarithm gives $
abla\log T=-
abla\log N_\xi=-a$.

Evaluating the constant identity of step 2.1 at any supplied $x_{\rm ref}$ yields $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, this is the reference local temperature. Under $\xi\mapsto b\xi$, $N_\xi\mapsto bN_\xi$ and therefore $T_K\mapsto bT_K$; the formula $T=T_K/N_\xi$ leaves $T$ unchanged.

citations.quote:
On a nonempty connected open set $O$ in the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], select one smooth future timelike Killing field $\xi$ and one smooth scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ in kelvins. Its dimensionless lapse and selected observer congruence are

$$N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0,\qquad u:=\xi/N_\xi.$$

Thus $g(u,u)=-1$ and the physical four-velocity is $cu$ in the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. A reference normalization of $\xi$ is part of the selected model. The local temperature $T$ is assigned to this comoving observer congruence; it is not a coordinate temperature or a value assigned to every observer.

Adopt the inverse-temperature vector

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},$$

where $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, and assume that this field is Killing on $O$. In this item, a selected stationary thermal equilibrium means precisely this adopted bath, observer congruence, positive proper-temperature field, and Killing condition on $\beta$. The field $N_\xi T$ is not assumed constant here; its constancy is the conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]].

This is a model assumption, not a statement that every stationary geometry admits a thermal state or that every material realizes this bath. It asserts no complete Killing flow, KMS state, trace-class stress exponential, collision or thermalization law, Hawking or Unruh temperature, or empirical thermometer reading.

For a selected fixed-composition material branch, adopt the local state function and energy convention of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In that state map, $T>0$ is the derivative of the supplied energy per marker with respect to entropy per marker, and the chemical potential is $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$ in joules per marker. Rest energy stays in the energy convention used for $\mu$ and for any particle generator; a rest-energy subtraction made in a different convention must be tracked explicitly.

For particle exchange, select and declare one of these physical model protocols:

- **Finite-cell exchange.** Supply $r\ge1$ finitely many independent cells with open convex state domains $U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, coordinates $(E_i,n_i)$, and concave entropy functions $S_i\in C^1(U_i,\mathbb R)$. Here $E_i$ is in joules, $n_i$ is a continuous dimensionless particle-number coordinate, and $S_i$ is in joules per kelvin. Fix dimensionless lapse values $N_i>0$, a common charge $q$ in coulombs, and potential values $\Phi_i$ in volts in a stated common reference. Put $U=\prod_iU_i$ and $S_{\rm tot}=\sum_iS_i$. The adopted exchange conserves $\mathcal E=\sum_i(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i)$ and $\mathcal N=\sum_i n_i$. At a supplied feasible interior point $x^*\in U$, with these totals fixed and $\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)>0$ for every $i$, adopt the following equilibrium criterion: $DS_{\rm tot}(x^*)[h]=0$ for every $h=(\delta E_1,\delta n_1,\ldots,\delta E_r,\delta n_r)$ satisfying $\sum_i(N_i\delta E_i+q\Phi_i\delta n_i)=0$ and $\sum_i\delta n_i=0$. All such independent infinitesimal variations are admitted. Define $1/T_i=\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)$ and $\mu_i/T_i=-\partial_{n_i}S_i(x_i^*)$, so $T_i>0$ is in kelvins and $\mu_i$ is in joules per particle. This criterion is an adopted condition on any selected equilibrium point, not a consequence of conservation, an existence assertion, or a relaxation law. [[thm-tgr-finite-entropy-exchange-equilibrium]] supplies its conditional consequences. Identification of these variables with another material state map is an additional model identification, not inferred here.

- **Charged kinetic exchange.** On the selected stationary domain, supply a species of rest mass $m>0$, charge $q$, smooth local fields $T>0$ and $\mu$, a global smooth real potential $A$ with $F=dA$, and a smooth compensator $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Use the future massive shell, charged transport, and dimensionless exponential ansatz exactly as defined in [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Adopt whole-shell stationarity $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ as the exchange criterion. This is a model assumption on every future mass-shell momentum, not an assertion that collisions drive a gas to this ansatz.

The two protocols are separate model choices. This postulate does not derive either protocol from gravity, assert a global electrostatic potential when no single-valued symmetry compensator exists, establish a Gibbs state or material realization, or identify finite entropy variables with kinetic fields without an explicit model assumption.

Let $O$ be a connected domain with the stationary Lorentzian data, potential
$A$, field $F=dA$, Killing field $\xi$, lapse $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, future
unit stationary observer $u=\xi/N$, and charged transport on the future mass
shell from [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$,
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ for a smooth proper-temperature scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$,
and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ for a smooth chemical-potential scalar
$\mu:O\to\mathbb R$. Define $f(x,P)=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$. Without any global
potential-symmetry assumption,
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \beta\text{ is Killing and }d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F.$$

If, in addition, a global smooth compensator satisfies
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, define $\Phi_\xi=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)$.
Then the stationarity conditions above are equivalent to the existence of
constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$NT=T_K,\qquad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K},\qquad N\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K.$$
With $E_{\rm loc}:=-g(P,u)$ and
$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi$, the same exponent then has both forms
$$\zeta+g(\beta,P)=-\frac{E_{\rm loc}-\mu}{k_BT} =-\frac{H_\xi-\mu_K}{k_BT_K}.$$
Here $N$ is dimensionless, $T,T_K$ are kelvins, $\mu,\mu_K,E_{\rm loc},H_\xi$
are joules per particle, $\Phi_\xi$ is volts, $q$ is coulombs, and
$\beta\cdot P$ and $\zeta$ are dimensionless. All claims are mathematical
conditional deductions from the displayed smooth data; no equilibrium state,
particle ensemble, or physical realization is asserted to exist.

Let $r\ge1$ be finite. For each cell $i=1,\ldots,r$, let $U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^2$
be open and convex, with coordinates $(E_i,n_i)$, and let
$S_i\in C^1(U_i,\mathbb R)$ be concave. The coordinates may be assigned SI
dimensions $[E_i]=\mathrm J$, $[n_i]=1$, and $[S_i]=\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; the
particle-number coordinate is a continuous thermodynamic variable. Fix
constants $N_i>0$ (dimensionless), $\Phi_i\in\mathbb R$ (volts), and a common
charge $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). Define
$$\mathcal E(x):=\sum_{i=1}^r(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i),\qquad \mathcal N(x):=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,\qquad S_{\rm tot}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^rS_i(E_i,n_i).$$
For a supplied feasible interior point $x^*\in U:=\prod_iU_i$, let
$A:\mathbb R^{2r}\to\mathbb R^2$ be the linear map whose rows are the
coefficients of $(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)$. Call $x^*$ stationary under
independent exchange variations when
$DS_{\rm tot}(x^*)[h]=0$ for every $h\in\ker A$. Assume
$\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)>0$ and define
$$\frac1{T_i}:=\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*),\qquad \frac{\mu_i}{T_i}:=-\partial_{n_i}S_i(x_i^*).$$
Then $x^*$ is stationary if and only if there are constants $T_K>0$ and
$\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that, for every cell,
$$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K.$$
If each $S_i$ is concave, every such stationary point is a global maximizer of
$S_{\rm tot}$ on the feasible set in $U$. If each $S_i$ is strictly concave,
that maximizer is unique whenever it exists. No existence or boundary
attainment of a stationary point is asserted. These are finite-dimensional
conditional deductions; the coefficients $N_i,\Phi_i$ are inputs, not
predictions about a physical system.

derivations.claim: In the charged kinetic branch, [F1] supplies the connected stationary Lorentzian carrier and [A1] supplies the global smooth potential-compensator condition. By [F2], the selected model's $T,\mu$ define the exact exponential ansatz and its adopted equilibrium condition is $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ on the whole future massive shell. Thus the charged branch matches the smooth-field, positive-mass, connected-domain, global-compensator, and full-shell hypotheses of [F3].

In the finite-cell branch, [A2] supplies exactly the finite state domains, differentiable concave entropies, positive energy derivatives, feasible interior point, and independent variations preserving the two affine constraints. By [F4], the temperatures and chemical potentials used here are defined from those entropy derivatives, so the branch matches the finite-dimensional theorem's inputs.

Apply [F3] under the conditions checked in step 1.1. It gives global constants $T_K>0,\mu_K$ with $N_\xi T=T_K$, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and $N_\xi\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K$. The global compensation hypothesis is essential for the last constant; stationarity of $F$ alone would only make $\iota_\xi F$ closed.

Apply [F4] to the point of step 1.2. It gives constants $T_K>0,\mu_K$ satisfying $N_iT_i=T_K$ and $N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$ for every cell. Its concavity and strict-concavity conclusions give the stated maximum and uniqueness qualifications; no stationary point is asserted to exist.

In the charged branch, replacing $\Phi_\xi$ by $\Phi_\xi+C$ changes the multiplier to $\mu_K+qC$ by the exact reference convention in [F3], so the relation and the exponent convention remain unchanged. In the finite branch, replacing every $\Phi_i$ by $\Phi_i+C$ adds $qC\sum_i n_i$ to the energy constraint; since $\sum_i n_i$ is separately fixed, the feasible set is unchanged, and the displayed relation is preserved by $\mu_K\mapsto\mu_K+qC$. Setting $q=0$ removes the potential term in either branch.

Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

derivations.claim: The metric coefficients are independent of $x^0$, so $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ is Killing. Its norm is $g(\xi,\xi)=-f(r)$, and $f(r)>0$ exactly on $r>r_s$. Therefore it is future timelike on this domain and $N_\xi=\sqrt{f(r)}$.

The connected exterior, smooth positive lapse, selected stationary bath, and Killing inverse-temperature field meet [F1]. Hence $N_\xi T=T_K$ throughout the exterior, so $T=T_K/\sqrt f$. Since $N_\xi\to1$ as $r\to\infty$, write this reference constant as $T_\infty=T_K$.

From $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$ in [F1], $a_r=\partial_r(\tfrac12\log f)=r_s/(2r^2f)$. Raising the index with $g^{rr}=f$ gives $a^r=r_s/(2r^2)$, and then $g_{ab}a^aa^b=f^{-1}(a^r)^2$, so $c^2|a|=c^2r_s/(2r^2\sqrt f)=G_Nm_s/(r^2\sqrt f)$.

Put $z=r_s/r$. For $0<z\le z_0<1$, Taylor's theorem at $z=0$ for $\varphi(z)=(1-z)^{-1/2}$ gives $\varphi(z)=1+z/2+\varphi''(\theta z)z^2/2$ for some $\theta\in(0,1)$, and $\varphi''(y)=\tfrac34(1-y)^{-5/2}$. Thus the remainder is at most $\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}z^2$. Since $z/2=G_Nm_s/(c^2r)$, this proves the displayed bound.

Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

Let $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and let $\mathcal H:=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0,\mathbb C)$ be the complex square-summable sequences with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{n\ge0}x_n\overline{y_n}$, linear in its first argument. Let $e_n$ be the sequence with value $1$ at $n$ and $0$ elsewhere. Write $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ for the bounded complex-linear operators on $\mathcal H$, with operator norm $\|B\|:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le1}\|Bx\|_2$; for $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, $C^*$ is its bounded Hilbert-space adjoint, characterized by $\langle Cx,y\rangle=\langle x,C^*y\rangle$. A state on this operator algebra means a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(C^*C)\ge0$ for every $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Define the occupation-number operator
$$D(\mathcal N):=\left\{x\in\mathcal H:\sum_{n\ge0}n^2|x_n|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad (\mathcal Nx)_n:=nx_n.$$
For a densely defined operator $T$ on this space, use the adjoint relation
$$D(T^\dagger):=\left\{y\in\mathcal H:\exists z\in\mathcal H\ \forall x\in D(T),\ \langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle\right\},\qquad T^\dagger y:=z.$$
The representing $z$ is unique when $D(T)$ is dense; here “self-adjoint” means $D(T^\dagger)=D(T)$ and $T^\dagger x=Tx$ on that domain.

Let $\epsilon>0$ be in joules, $m\in\mathbb Z$ a dimensionless azimuthal mode number, $\Omega\in\mathbb R$ an angular velocity in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. Set
$$H:=\epsilon\mathcal N,\qquad J:=\hbar m\mathcal N,\qquad a:=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega.$$ 
For $m\ne0$, $J$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $m=0$, $J$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. The operator $H$ has energy units J, $J$ has angular-momentum units J s, and $a$ has energy units J, so $\Omega J$ also has units J. Define $K_0:=H-\Omega J$ on the common domain $D(\mathcal N)$ and let $K:=\overline{K_0}$ be its operator closure. For $a\ne0$, $K=a\mathcal N$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $a=0$, $K$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. Thus $K$ is the self-adjoint closure of the rotating generator $H-\Omega J$, including at the zero threshold. Then $\mathcal N$, $H$, $J$ and $K$ are self-adjoint on the stated domains.

Define the one-mode occupation partition sum by
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty e^{-\beta_Kan}\in[0,+\infty].$$
It is the diagonal trace of the positive Gibbs weights in the occupation basis whenever the sum is finite. This sum is finite exactly when $a=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega>0$, in which case
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a)=\frac{1}{1-e^{-\beta_Ka}}.$$
For $a>0$, the weights $p_n=Z_{\beta_K}(a)^{-1}e^{-\beta_Kan}$ sum to one and define the diagonal Gibbs functional
$$\omega_a(B):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_n\langle Be_n,e_n\rangle,\qquad B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H).$$
The proof shows that this is a state in the stated sense. For $a\le0$, the occupation partition sum diverges, so no normalized Gibbs state of this trace form exists. This is a single bosonic mode calculation; it constructs no continuum field state or rotating-spacetime equilibrium.

derivations.claim: The Rindler metric is independent of $x^0$, so $\xi_R$ is Killing. Its norm is $g(\xi_R,\xi_R)=-(a_0x/c^2)^2<0$ on $x>0$, hence $N_R=a_0x/c^2$. Differentiating $\log N_R$ gives $a_x=1/x$, whose metric norm is $1/x$.

In the rotating Minkowski metric, $\partial_{x^0}$ and $\partial_\phi$ are Killing fields and $\Omega$ is constant, so their displayed linear combination $\xi_\Omega$ is Killing. Its squared norm is $-1+\Omega^2r^2/c^2$, which is negative exactly for $r<c/|\Omega|$ when $\Omega\ne0$; therefore $N_\Omega=\sqrt{1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2}$.

For a nonconstant angular velocity, the coordinate formula for the Lie derivative gives $(\mathcal L_\xi g)_{r\phi}=g_{\phi\phi}\partial_r(\Omega/c)=r^2\Omega'(r)/c$. Thus if $\Omega'(r)\ne0$, this field is not Killing and the selected stationary theorem does not apply.

By [F1] and [A2], the selected Rindler bath has $T_R=T_K/N_R=T_Kc^2/(a_0x)$ and physical proper acceleration $c^2|a|=c^2/x$. The point $x_{\rm ref}=c^2/a_0$ has $N_R=1$, so it provides the stated reference normalization.

Applying [F1] on that selected timelike domain yields $T_\Omega=T_K/N_\Omega$. Differentiating $\log N_\Omega$ gives $a_r=-\Omega^2r/[c^2(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)]$. Since $g_{rr}=1$, its physical magnitude is $c^2|a_r|=\gamma^2\Omega^2r$. At the light cylinder the norm tends to zero and the timelike-field hypothesis of [F1] fails.

Under [A3], the mode generator has coefficient $a=\epsilon-\hbar j\Omega$ in the exact occupation model of [F2]. Applying [F2] gives a finite trace exactly for $a>0$. This condition is logically separate from the geometric timelike-domain condition in step 1.2 and supplies no continuum-field conclusion.
